# dsh-web-lan-access
**English** | 简体中文
LAN / remote access support for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI.
Bind every interface with one command, reach the GUI from a LAN IP, a Tailscale IP, or a VPN address
, and keep Host-backed settings working on the remote page.
## Compatibility
| dsh | plugin | notes |

| **0.2.2-rc.1** | **1.4.x** | current; verified end to end |
| 0.2.1-rc.x | 1.4.x | verified end to

end |
| 0.2.0-rc.x | 1.3.x | shipped webserver still accepted `0.0.0.0` |
| ≤ 0.1.7 | 1.3.x | no wi

c.x | 1.3.x | shipped webserver still accepted `0.0.0.0` |
| ≤ 0.1.7 | 1.3.x | no wildcard ban yet |
Version 1.4.0 is the release that tracks dsh 0.2.1's stricter webserver. See Why 1.4.0 had to change
if you are upgrading from 1.3.x.
## The problem
Three separate things stand between a remote browser and a working GUI:
**1. The listener binds loopback only.** `dsh web` defaults to `127.0.0.1`, and from 0.2.1 the CLI r
ejects a wildcard host outright:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**2. The `/api` fence rejects unknown authorities.** Every request must name a loopback host, the li
stener's own bind literal, or a declared `trustedHosts` entry. A wildcard bind has no literal of its
own — `0.0.0.0` matches no request `Host` — so the page shell loads but every `/api` call returns *
*403** and sessions never appear.
**3. Host-backed settings are gated on `isLoopback`.** `client-connection` derives `isLoopback: tran
sport?.ownsHost === true`, and client plugins consult that fact before reaching Host surfaces. A pag
e served from a LAN or Tailscale address is not loopback by hostname, so the Models and plugin setti
ngs pages stay empty even after authentication succeeds.
## The fix
Two small pieces, both reversible.
### A replacement `webserver` row
`lib/webserver.js` subclasses `@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver` and changes exactly two things:
- **`Config`** delegates to the shipped schema and rescues *only* the wildcard rejection. A non-lite
ral host, a port out of range, or a missing port still fail exactly as before — the relaxation is on

e error message wide.
- **`getOrigin()`** never returns a wildcard origin. The parent builds its URL
from the bind address, which would yield `http://0.0.0.0:3080` — an address no browser can dial. A
wildcard listener reports loopback instead, and `--public-url` still overrides the advertised root u
listener reports loopback instead, and `--public-url` still overrides the advertised root upstream.
Everything else — the service name, routes, index taps, TLS handling, gzip, listener lifecycle — is
inherited untouched.
### A `/api` fence widened from the live interface list
The bundle patch derives `trustedHosts` from every non-internal IPv4 the host currently has, so LAN,
Tailscale (`100.x`), and VPN addresses are all accepted without per-IP configuration.
### A bootstrap script for Host ownership
Injected as the first script in `<head>`, before the boot manifest and shell entry, through the webs
erver's official index-tap extension point (`webServer.tapIndex`). It declares `ownsHost: true` whil
e keeping the ordinary HTTP `fetch` transport, and leaves a transport supplied by another shell unto
ing the ordinary HTTP `fetch` transport, and leaves a transport supplied by another shell untouched.
> **What 1.4.0 removed:** the `crypto.randomUUID` polyfill. From 0.2.1 DSH mints UUIDs through `@dee
pseek-ai/dsh-util-crypto`, which is built on `crypto.getRandomValues` — available on insecure origin
s — so a plain-HTTP LAN page needs no patch to render. The old polyfill is gone because the bug it w
orked around no longer exists.
## Why 1.4.0 had to change
Through 1.3.x this plugin worked by writing `host: '0.0.0.0'` into the shipped `webserver` row's con
fig. That stopped working in 0.2.1 for two independent reasons:
1. The webserver's own schema now rejects wildcard addresses, so the row fails validation and the bo

ot aborts with `3 required plugins did not activate`.
2. A patch cannot retarget a row's `name` — ap
p-boot skips any patch whose `name` differs from the target's — so the row could not be swapped for
a custom module in place.
1.4.0 therefore disables the shipped row (`disabled: true`, which startup auditing skips) and mounts
the subclass under a new id. A second breakage came from the same upgrade: `web-app` no longer prov
ides the `webRuntime` service, so the old `ctx.webRuntime?.trustedHosts` expression threw `cannot ge
t property "webRuntime" without inject`. The fence list is now derived directly from `os.networkInte
"webRuntime" without inject`. The fence list is now derived directly from `os.networkInterfaces()`.
## Install
### Method 1: Ask your DSH Agent (Easiest 🤖)

Send this repo URL directly to your DSH chat with the instruction:
> "Install this plugin for me: ht
tps://github.com/AcidGr/dsh-web-lan-access"
Your DSH Agent will automatically install the package and configure it in the background.

## Security warning
Binding `0.0.0.0` exposes the DSH authentication surface to **every** reachable interface, including
addresses you may not have considered — container bridges, VPN tunnels, and any other network the h
ost is attached to. `trustedHosts` is an Origin/Host fence, not identity; DSH separately authenticat
to. `trustedHosts` is an Origin/Host fence, not identity; DSH separately authenticates the browser.
This plugin deliberately relaxes a restriction the DSH maintainers added on purpose:
> binding every interface would expose remote code execution to the network
Use it only on trusted networks, restrict the port with a firewall (e.g. `ufw allow from 192.168.0.0
/16`), or front it with Tailscale or an authenticated reverse proxy. If a single interface is enough
, prefer plain `dsh web --host <ip>` — it needs no plugin, and the fence auto-trusts the bind litera
prefer plain `dsh web --host <ip>` — it needs no plugin, and the fence auto-trusts the bind literal.
Because this plugin depends on the webserver's schema and URL-building internals, a future DSH relea
se may break it again. Check the compatibility table before upgrading.
